reasoning.reconstruction: Write Phi=d^(-1/2)sum_i e_i tensor e_i in the same fixed orthonormal basis on both copies. (X tensor I)Phi=d^(-1/2)sum_(j,i) X_(j,i)e_j tensor e_i. The coefficient of e_j tensor e_i in (I tensor X^T)Phi is (X^T)_(i,j)=X_(j,i), so the vectors agree for every complex linear X, not only a Hermitian or unitary one. With X=U, applying I tensor conjugate(U) gives (U tensor conjugate(U))Phi=(I tensor conjugate(U)*U^T)Phi. Taking entrywise conjugates of U U†=I yields conjugate(U)*U^T=I, hence exact vector invariance, not merely phase invariance.
reasoning.boundaries_and_conventions: d>=1 is explicit, so the normalized sum exists; d1 phases cancel exactly. Transpose/conjugation refer to the basis used in Phi, not to a basis-free transpose of a linear map. If bases change, the entangled representative and conjugation convention must be changed together. Unitarity is used only in part(b); part(a) is valid for all X. For d2,U=diag(1,i), U tensor U sends Phi to(|00>-|11>)/sqrt(2), which is not the original vector or even the same ray. Omitting conjugation is genuinely false, not a relabeling.

reasoning.valid_covariance_reconstruction: In Tbar(V^tensorN X(V†)^tensorN), group the inner unitaries as U V, then set W=U V, so U=W V† and U†=V W†. The outside factors become V^tensorM (W†)^tensorM and W^tensorM(V†)^tensorM. Normalized Haar integration is unchanged, so pulling V outside proves exactly Tbar(V^tensorN X(V†)^tensorN)=V^tensorM Tbar(X)(V†)^tensorM. Each integrand is a unitary-channel conjugation of T, hence Tbar is CPTP. The substitution uses RIGHT translation, not bare left translation. On compact U(d) right invariance follows from uniqueness of normalized left Haar: the right-translated measure is again normalized and left invariant. The primary source explicitly lists both in Eq3.3/Proposition3.39.
reasoning.exact_exposition_issue: The reference's final sentence says covariance pins down Tbar on Sym^M up to a single parameter. What follows from Schur in the source is narrower: for the invariant INPUT tau_N=Pi_N/d_N, covariance makes OUTPUT Tbar(tau_N) invariant, and its symmetric M block is a scalar Pi_M/d_M times its mass lambda. For a general X the output is only covariant, not invariant. With d2,N=M1,T the identity channel, Tbar=T and Tbar(|0><0|)=|0><0|, which is not a scalar on Sym^1=C^2. This directly refutes any scalar-output reading for arbitrary X.
reasoning.multiplicity_boundary: Nor does unitary commutation alone force scalars on every isotypic component: it permits arbitrary matrices on the multiplicity factors. For d2,M3, the U(2) spin-one-half sector has multiplicity2 and a factor permutation acts nontrivially on that multiplicity while commuting with U^tensor3. Additional permutation commutation, as in415, removes that freedom. A channel is a superoperator intertwining conjugation representations, not itself an ordinary endomorphism on one U(d) irrep to which Schur can be applied without specifying spaces.

reasoning.permutation_and_measurement_reconstructi: Because Q_pi rho^tensor n Q_pi†=rho^tensor n, replacing EVERY effect E_y of a POVM by its permutation average preserves each tr(E_y rho^tensor n) exactly, for every rho. Positivity and sum_y E_y=I survive averaging. The Schur-Weyl orthogonal block projections P_lambda are positive, mutually orthogonal and sum to I; both commuting group actions preserve each block, hence [P_lambda,Q_pi]=[P_lambda,U^tensor n]=0. A POVM invariant under BOTH actions has effects E_y=sum_lambda a_(y,lambda)P_lambda with a>=0 and sum_y a_(y,lambda)=1; it is implemented by weak Schur sampling followed by that stochastic classical postprocessing.
reasoning.unitary_wlog_requires_performance_contra: The spectrum's invariance does not imply that a given estimator's effect probabilities are already basis invariant, or that Haar twirling preserves them pointwise. A correct WLOG statement is about a UNIFORM spectrum-only guarantee or unitarily invariant worst-case loss: if an estimator has error at most delta for every rho at a given spectral tolerance eps, averaging its conjugates preserves that uniform guarantee, because every conjugate has the same target spectrum. Likewise a Haar-invariant prior gives equal Bayes risk. The twirl may improve some orientations and worsen others. Neither uniform accuracy/loss nor a prior is explicitly specified in this exact question/empty assumptions; its request to explain precisely WLOG is not discharged by saying the invariant estimator is natural.
reasoning.explicit_nonpreservation_witness: For n1,d2, take the valid effect E=|0><0|, with outcomes assigned any two spectrum estimates, and rho=diag(4/5,1/5). Its probability is4/5; for the basis-swapped conjugate of rho it is1/5 despite the same spectrum. Haar-averaged E is I/2, with probability1/2 on each. Thus no claim that ALL spectrum-labeled measurements retain their original statistics under unitary averaging can be true. Weak Schur sampling at n1 has only lambda=(1), so a fixed classical postprocessing of it cannot reproduce this orientation-sensitive pair of probabilities.
